audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo del 3.14%, Shanghai in calo del 2.04%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dell'1.08%, il VIX è sceso dello 0.69%. Il rendimento del US 10Y è in calo del 2.04%, al 4.57%. L'oro è pressoché invariato, a 4530 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio Brent è in rialzo dello 0.74%, a 105.8 dollari. I BTP 10Y sono stabili al 3.73%.

La situazione in Medio Oriente continua a influenzare i prezzi del petrolio, con due tanker diretti in Cina che attraversano lo Stretto di Hormuz. La guerra e le tensioni commerciali rimangono una preoccupazione per i mercati.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi. Tuttavia, diversi funzionari della Fed hanno suggerito di rimuovere il segnale di taglio dei tassi a breve termine.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 
  Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantasettemila dollari, con una variazione del +0,55%. 
  Tuttavia, i flussi ETF mostrano un deflusso di 70,5 milioni di dollari. 
  Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato da una generale cautela degli investitori.

  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum è pressoché invariata a duemilacentotrentacinque dollari, con un +0,06%. 
  Solana mostra un buon andamento con un +2,15% a ottantasei dollari e settantaquattro centesimi. 
  Anche BNB registra un +1,56% a seicentocinquantaquattro dollari e trenta centesimi.

  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 29, in zona Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 3.14%, while Shanghai fell 2.04%. This suggests a positive opening for European markets. The S&P 500 closed up 1.08%, and the VIX dropped 0.69%. The US 10Y yield is down 2.04% to 4.57%. Gold is essentially flat at $4,530 per ounce. The situation in the Middle East continues to influence oil prices, with two tankers heading to China crossing the Strait of Hormuz. War and trade tensions remain a concern for markets. Among altcoins, Ethereum is essentially flat at $2,135, up 0.06%. Thanks for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Learning monetary policy strategies at the effective lower bound with sudden surprises
articles.snippet: by Spencer Krane, Leonardo Melosi, Matthias Rottner We examine how private sector agents might learn a new monetary strategy introduced while policy rates are at their effective lower bound (ELB) in an environment with large inflationary and deflationary shocks. We consider the adoption of a new asymmetric average inflation targeting rule aimed at countering the disinflationary bias imparted by the ELB. The most crucial time for learning runs from when rates would be near liftoff under the old strategy through early liftoff under the new rule. Recessionary shocks during this time could delay learning while large inflationary shocks could outright stop it, inhibiting the ability of the new strategy to address the costs associated with the ELB.

articles.title_en: Learning monetary policy strategies at the effective lower bound with sudden surprises

articles.title: How to Win a Trade War: Book launch and discussion with Bown and Keynes
articles.snippet: Soumaya Keynes and Chad P. Bown discuss their new book How to Win a Trade War, available for pre-order. Trade wars are here to stay, and refusing to engage in the fight is no longer an option. President Donald Trump's tariff announcements can crash markets and sour decades-long alliances. China's export restrictions on rare earths could bring the West's car production to a crashing halt. Curbs on trade in cutting-edge chips could determine who wins the artificial intelligence (AI) race. From identifying supply chain vulnerabilities to installing stockpiles, subsidies, and trade restrictions,…

articles.snippet: The Climate Briefing: Oil and gas producers in the Gulf: a deep dive (part 2 of 2) Audio thilton.drupal 20 May 2026 Anna and Bhargabi speak with Robin Mills (Qamar Energy), Jessica Obeid (New Energy Consult) and Neil Quilliam about how the countries around the Gulf are approaching – and may be impacted by – the energy transition. All eyes are currently on the Gulf due to the US-Israeli war on Iran and the disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz. In this two-part series, the Climate Briefing co-hosts and their guests take a deep dive into the region, which plays a crucial role in the global supply of oil and gas. The first part of the series (released on 21 April) delved into the history of the region, addressing questions such as: How did the Gulf countries become such dominant fossil fuel

articles.title: The Gulf’s Post-OPEC Order
articles.snippet: The United Arab Emirates’ decision to leave OPEC is the clearest expression yet of its desire to break from the Saudi-led regional order. The result could be a more fragmented Middle East marked by intensifying rivalries among Gulf powers, widening proxy conflicts, and chronic instability.

articles.title: Europe’s Dangerous Hunger Games for American Troops
articles.snippet: Every time reports emerge about a potential reduction of U.S. forces or capabilities in Europe, the old continent falls into the same cycle of anxiety and panic. The same applies to announcements about delayed or suspended deployments, planned rotations, or broader force posture reviews.A brief historical reminder here is necessary. The 2014 Wales Defense Investment Pledge is still often misunderstood in Europe as little more than an American demand for higher defense spending. In reality, it reflected something broader already taking shape in Washington: the expectation that Europe would gradually assume far greater responsibility for conventional defense on its own continent. The post Europe’s Dangerous Hunger Games for American Troops appeared first on War on the Rocks .
